sourceFacts.B1ClippingResult: Computed mobile face clip-path none through existing production CSS; fold clipping remains unchanged

measurementProtocol.environment: Windows desktop, headless Google Chrome 154 and Playwright WebKit 26.0. DPR 3, mobile/touch emulation.
measurementProtocol.inputs: 95 observed RAF callbacks; identical 46-position forward and 46-position reverse scroll sequence from territory .30 to .60. 90 delivered scroll events and 88 actual render updates per run.
measurementProtocol.viewportPreparation: At y=0, width changes by -50px and returns to target. Exercises the existing production recompose path after page and fonts settle; prevents stale territory measurements from dominating Paint comparison.
measurementProtocol.instrumentation: Transient CSSStyleDeclaration.setProperty counter, scroll listener, existing snapshot samples, Chromium CDP tracing/layer tree. Probes removed after each measurement. No diagnostics loaded by owner previews.
measurementProtocol.chromiumOrder: B0/B1 first trial, B1/B0 second trial
limitations: Synthetic input is not finger scrolling; this does not measure async iOS scroll delivery.
RAF callback intervals are not presentation times or real iPhone GPU timings.
Trace Paint/Raster durations include the whole homepage; Raster sums span parallel worker tasks.
Trace recording and probes have measurement overhead.
Windows WebKit has extremely slow rendering in this environment; absolute results are not transferable.
WebKit longtask observation and GPU Paint/Composite trace are unavailable.
One initial Chromium landscape B0 run had unusually long frames; it did not reproduce in the reversed-order repeat.
B1 changes occlusion and visible pixel area. A perceived benefit alone could reflect removal of a high-contrast clip edge.
Fresh-load cached territory may differ from settled DOM position; this is pre-existing and identical in B0/B1, not altered by this experiment.

decision.B1b: NOT REQUIRED: scroll/RAF/render cadence recorded in the same transient observation
decision.reason: Dynamic clipping creates measurable extra Chromium face Paint work, but no consistent frame-cadence improvement; Windows WebKit gets slower. Evidence does not establish that a movement/clipping wrapper will fix real-iPhone jitter.
decision.realDeviceUnknown: Await owner B0/B1 comparison on iPhone Chrome/WebKit. Do not promote A or B1.
